title: Prospective study on the influence of multibracket appliances on digital denatl cast analysis
summary:
The three-dimensional measurement and evaluation of models of the upper and lower jaw is an integral part of orthodontic diagnostics and treatment planning. It thus has a significant influence on the selection of the most suitable therapy for the individual patient. The current gold standard, manual analysis on plaster models, is increasingly being replaced by digitalisation in dentistry/orthodontics. For example, scanners and corresponding software programmes are now available and can be used to perform such a model analysis digitally. Whether digital model analysis achieves the gold standard in terms of measurement accuracy should therefore be investigated. 
Model analysis is not only necessary before the start of therapy, but also during therapy to monitor the progress of treatment with fixed braces (brackets). However, brackets could negatively influence the scanning process and subsequent processing in the software, thus affecting the accuracy of the measurements. Although the influence of brackets on scans has already been investigated, an analysis of the effect of brackets on digital model analysis is still lacking – especially in the ‘OnyxCeph’ software.
In view of the insufficient studies and data available, a prospective clinical study is to be conducted to examine whether brackets have a negative influence on the digital model analysis compared to models of patients without brackets. Only patients who got fixed braces for medical reasons will be considered.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- all age groups, but permanent set of teeth 6-6 
- all ethnic groups 
- all malocclusions and dysgnathias with the exception of cleft lip and palate  
- vestibular multi-bracket appliance (at least 50% of the dental arch)
Exclusion criteria:
- syndromes/ cleft lip and palate/ genetic diseases
- patients with oligodontia
- ceramic brackets
